symbols.meaning: natural gradient of the objective function J with respect to θ
expected fitness or objective function under the distribution, E_θ[f(x)]
plain (vanilla) gradient of the objective function J with respect to θ
Fisher information matrix (Riemannian metric tensor g)

properties.why: The natural gradient direction is defined using the Riemannian Fisher information metric, making the update direction invariant to the choice of distribution parameterization
Pre-multiplying by the inverse Fisher matrix renormalizes update magnitudes with respect to uncertainty, mitigating premature convergence and oscillations on ridges and plateaus
The Fisher information matrix is the covariance matrix of the score functions (log-derivatives ∇_θ log π(x|θ)), as the expectation of the score function is zero
The Fisher information metric is symmetric and positive (semi)definite, appearing as the Hessian in the second-order Taylor expansion of D_KL[P(θ_0) || P(θ)] around θ_0

assumptions.assumption: The Fisher information matrix F is non-singular and invertible
assumptions.breaks_when: The parameterization is redundant, or the sample estimate of F is rank-deficient due to sample size λ being smaller than parameter dimension d

assumptions.assumption: The distribution π(x|θ) is smooth and continuously differentiable with respect to θ
assumptions.breaks_when: The density function has non-differentiable points or boundaries that depend discontinuously on θ

assumptions.assumption: The log-derivatives (score functions) ∇_θ log π(x|θ) exist and have finite second-order moments
assumptions.breaks_when: The distribution has heavy tails or support such that the expected outer product of log-derivatives diverges

failure_modes.mode: Singular or ill-conditioned Fisher information matrix
failure_modes.signature: Matrix inversion failure, numerical instability, or exploded parameter updates
failure_modes.cause: Overparameterization, zero curvature in certain parameter directions, or empirical estimation of F with fewer samples λ than parameter dimension d

failure_modes.signature: Out-of-memory errors and prohibitive per-iteration computational runtime
failure_modes.cause: Storing an O(d^2) matrix and performing an O(d^3) matrix inversion when parameter dimension d is very large

failure_modes.mode: Sampling variance in Monte Carlo estimation
failure_modes.signature: Erratic optimization trajectories, noisy updates, or premature convergence
failure_modes.cause: Using too small a population/sample size λ to accurately estimate the score-function expectation and Fisher matrix
